what: Dharmsalas in charge of an ascetic (usually Udasi) endowed with land; he feeds the poor, keeps langar going and reads the Granth; the head is guru and mahant, disciples chelas, forming a college
quote: Where, as in most cases, the occupant is an Udasi, he or one of his disciples (chela) also reads the Granth or Sikh scriptures.

what: Udasis: Sikh ascetics of a sect founded by Srichand; mostly Jat by origin; chela chosen from Jats; live in Sikh and Hindu villages; head called mahant; celibate, though some families (e.g. Jaspal Bangar) marry
quote: The TJdasIs are Sikh ascetics of a sect founded by the eldest son of Guru Nanak (Srichand).

what: Large langars: Jaspal Bangar held by a married family of Udasi faqirs (about 800 acres endowment; mahant Partab Das); Heran langar held by an Udasi ascetic (late mahant Gursarn Das fed thousands in famine of 1862)
quote: There is also a large langar at Jaspal Hangar, near Ludhiana, which is kept by a family of tldasi faqirs, whoso custom is also to marry.
